options.name: The Tumbler
options.subtitle: Rotating Sieve
options.description: Motorized rotating sieve/grate in lid; items pass through one-by-one; high-speed camera captures during fall
options.whyNonObvious: Gravity + rotation = natural separation (no complex vision needed)

risks.mitigation: Jam detection sensor + easy clear mechanism

options.howItWorks: User dumps food waste onto rotating sieve grate. As the sieve rotates (20-60 RPM), items naturally separate and fall through gaps one at a time. High-speed camera captures each item during the ~300ms freefall through the sieve. Weight sensors validate classification. Items land in standard collection bin below.

options.name: The Cascade
options.subtitle: Multi-Stage Conveyor
options.description: Short inclined conveyor belt spreads items; camera captures at viewing zone
options.whyNonObvious: Converts instantaneous dump into temporal spread
options.howItWorks: Waste falls onto short inclined conveyor belt. Belt moves at ~6 inches/second, naturally spreading items as they travel due to different rolling/sliding rates. Camera captures spread items at dedicated viewing zone with controlled lighting. Items cascade off belt end into collection bin.

options.name: The Kaleidoscope
options.subtitle: Mirror Multi-Angle
options.description: Single high-res camera + precision angled mirrors = 4-6 simultaneous views
options.whyNonObvious: Light physics replaces multiple cameras; single failure point
options.howItWorks: Single high-resolution camera mounted above bin. Precision angled mirrors arranged around bin opening capture 4-6 simultaneous views of the waste pile in a single frame. Software separates views and reconstructs multi-angle understanding. All views perfectly synchronized (same exposure).

options.name: The Listener
options.subtitle: Acoustic Sensing
options.description: 4-8 MEMS microphones capture impact sounds; ML trained on acoustic signatures
options.whyNonObvious: Different physics channel - doesn't care about occlusion; $5/mic

risks.mitigation: Trigger-based capture only during dump events

options.howItWorks: Array of 4-8 MEMS microphones arranged around bin opening. When items are dumped, each makes distinct impact sound (splat for wet, clatter for hard, thud for soft). ML model trained on acoustic signatures classifies material types. Time-of-arrival differences provide spatial information. Fused with vision for high accuracy.

options.name: The Photo Booth
options.subtitle: Drop-Through Tunnel
options.description: Vertical tube with cameras around circumference; items imaged during freefall
options.whyNonObvious: Gravity does sequencing for free; zero moving parts
options.howItWorks: Vertical transparent tube (12-18 inches) between dump opening and bin. Items fall through tube past multiple cameras positioned around circumference. High-speed imaging captures each item in freefall (natural separation). Breakbeam sensors trigger capture. 3D shape reconstructed from multiple simultaneous angles.

options.name: The Heat Map
options.subtitle: Thermal Differential
options.description: LWIR thermal camera + RGB; fresh waste has distinct thermal signature
options.whyNonObvious: Thermal contrast makes segmentation easier; works in any lighting

risks.mitigation: Best for hot food operations (delis, bakeries)

options.howItWorks: LWIR (Long-Wave Infrared) thermal camera mounted alongside RGB camera. Fresh waste has thermal signature different from bin/existing waste. Hot cooked food clearly distinct from cold produce. Temperature decay rate provides additional diagnostic (meat vs vegetable). Fused with RGB for comprehensive classification.

options.name: The Fingerprinter
options.subtitle: NIR/SWIR Spectral
options.description: Near-infrared captures material composition (water, sugar, protein)
options.whyNonObvious: Identifies food by chemistry, not appearance; proven in agriculture

risks.mitigation: Start with NIR, SWIR for premium tier

options.howItWorks: NIR (Near-Infrared) or SWIR (Short-Wave Infrared) camera captures beyond visible spectrum. Different organic materials have distinct spectral signatures based on water content, sugar, protein composition. Identifies material by chemical composition, not visual appearance. Can distinguish visually identical items (different apple varieties).

options.name: The Scanner
options.subtitle: Capacitive/RF Sensing
options.description: Capacitive antenna array in bin walls; measures dielectric properties
options.whyNonObvious: No line-of-sight needed - works through full occlusion

risks.mitigation: Must combine with vision for item-level ID

options.howItWorks: Capacitive or RF antenna array built into bin walls. Different foods have different dielectric properties based on water content. As items are dumped, array measures changes in capacitive field. Works even with full occlusion - measures entire bin volume. Tracks fill level automatically as bonus.

options.name: The Sculptor
options.subtitle: Structured Light Depth
options.description: IR pattern projection + camera for precise 3D reconstruction
options.whyNonObvious: Gets exact volume measurement, tracks changes between dumps
options.howItWorks: IR structured light projector casts known pattern onto waste. Camera captures distorted pattern. Real-time 3D surface reconstruction at high accuracy. Tracks changes between dumps to isolate new items. FOODCAM research achieved 94.4% portion size accuracy with this approach.

options.name: The Weighmaster
options.subtitle: Weight Dynamics
options.description: High-frequency load cell sampling (100+ Hz); impact curves are diagnostic
options.whyNonObvious: Weight signatures unique to item types; validates vision
options.howItWorks: High-precision load cell array under bin with high temporal resolution sampling (100+ Hz). As items land, weight increase curve has characteristic shape. Apple lands differently than bread. Multiple impacts can be separated temporally. Validates visual classification - if vision says 'apple' but weight says 0.1 oz, flag it.

options.name: The Polarizer
options.subtitle: Polarimetric Imaging
options.description: Camera with polarizing filter; organic vs synthetic materials differ
options.whyNonObvious: Cuts through glare/reflections; detects plastic contamination
options.howItWorks: Camera with rotating polarizing filter or dual-polarization sensor. Different materials reflect polarized light differently. Organic materials have distinct polarization signatures vs non-organic. Cuts through surface reflections that confuse standard cameras. Excellent for detecting plastic contamination.

options.name: The Penetrator
options.subtitle: Radar/Microwave Sensing
options.description: mmWave radar penetrates surface layer; sees through pile
options.whyNonObvious: Solves occlusion fundamentally; immune to visual confounders
options.howItWorks: Short-range mmWave radar or microwave sensor mounted on bin. Can penetrate surface layer to detect items underneath. Different materials have different radar cross-sections. Works through any visual obstruction - grease, condensation, piled items. Similar to automotive/robotics radar but miniaturized.
